# Cyril Lisle

## Overview

- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v3 c25 P43](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0043), [v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047)</sub>
- **Origin:** Portmaris  <sub>[v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047)</sub>

## Appearance

Cyril is an exceptionally handsome young man who possesses endearing good looks, dreamy dark eyes, and a deep, velvety smile. He speaks with an appealing cadence in his lovely voice.

_Sources: [v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047), [v3 c26 P18](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0018), [v3 c27 P36](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0036), [v3 c38 P44](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0044)_

## Personality

Cyril is romantic, intelligent, and courteous, maintaining respectful and constant manners that easily win over older figures. He expresses his emotions through poetry and elegant letters, though he lacks a sense of humor and real depth of substance. He carries himself with confidence, but he reacts with bitterness and hurt pride when his affection is rejected.

_Sources: [v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047), [v3 c26 P18](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0018), [v3 c27 P36](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0036), [v3 c28 P22](../source/v03-c28.md#nw-v03-c28-p0022), [v3 c38 P14](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0014), [v3 c38 P17](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0017), [v3 c38 P19](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0019), [v3 c38 P27](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0027), [v3 c39 P2](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0002)_

- Complete his Arts degree at Wexcombe  <sub>[v3 c25 P38](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0038)</sub>
- Marry Nell Harcourt  <sub>[v3 c36 P17](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0017), [v3 c38 P17](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0017)</sub>

## History

Cyril completed two years of study at Wexcombe before putting his degree on hold to spend two years in Europe accompanying his ill mother. He later returned to Wexcombe to finish his Junior year, where he met Nell Harcourt in the park during a rainstorm by sheltering her under his umbrella. He immediately pursued her, sending her long-stemmed roses, white orchids, and personal sonnets. Over two years at college, he corresponded with her twice weekly and escorted her to events, leading observers to assume an engagement was imminent. Before Convocation, he brought his mother and sisters to visit her circle, though his family initially harbored reservations. At the end of their term, Cyril took Nell to a small pavilion by the harbor and proposed marriage. Unexpectedly, Nell refused his proposal because she realized she did not love him. Heartbroken and bitter, Cyril accused her of ruining his life before bidding her farewell. His sister Dorothy later noted that while he suffered intensely following the rejection, he would eventually recover as he had in past romantic disappointments.

## Background by volume

- Completed his Freshman and Sophomore years at Wexcombe before pausing his studies  <sub>[v3 c25 P38](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0038)</sub>
- Spent two years traveling in Europe with his ill mother  <sub>[v3 c25 P38](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0038), [v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047)</sub>

## Quotes

> I have the impression that I do not fit in anywhere so far. Two years back, I completed my Freshman and Sophomore years at Wexcombe. I have resided in Europe from that time onward. At present, I have returned so that I can complete my Arts degree.  <sub>[v3 c25 P38](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0038)</sub>

> Your presence will soon be sought by my mother and sisters,  <sub>[v3 c36 P17](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0017)</sub>

> Then you have merely been entertaining yourself throughout these past two years?  <sub>[v3 c38 P25](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0025)</sub>

> My life has been destroyed by you,  <sub>[v3 c38 P27](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0027)</sub>

> Well then—farewell. It is beyond my comprehension—it is impossible for me to accept that you aren't the lady I thought you were. However, upbraiding one another is useless now. No other female will ever have my affection. I am grateful to you for your companionship, if nothing else. Farewell, Nell.  <sub>[v3 c38 P32](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0032)</sub>
